text: An open-source CLI for hillclimbing Agent Experience. Make your Skills, CLIs, SDKs, MCPs and docs easier for coding agents to discover and use. Gauge runs real agents against your product, captures where they get stuck, and lets your own coding agent test fixes before you publish them. The full loop runs locally with Docker and your existing agent subscriptions or API keys. No Gauge account required. Website · Documentation · Hosted Gauge · npm · Changelog Gauge runs and analyzes coding sessions to find the issues that coding agents run into. Common findings include: The right fix might change error messages, Skill content, help text, code, or documentation. The Gauge CLI lets you validate proposed fixes before release. Gauge is designed to be used by your coding agent. Point it at this repository and ask it to get started, or follow the steps below in the project you want to improve. You need Node.js 22.13+ , npm, Docker running Linux containers, and credentials for the agent you want to test. Gauge supports Claude Code, Codex, Pi, and OpenCode. It can use native Claude/Codex logins or API keys; agent usage is billed through your provider or subscription. npm install -g @withgauge/cli gauge local runtime pull Gauge downloads the published Docker image pinned to your CLI release. The image contains the agent harnesses and standard development tools. From your project directory (Git is optional): gauge init --local This creates a private .gauge/ workspace, including a SQLite database and local backend preference. Plain init changes no tracked files. Add --cases when you want shared Markdown cases: it also writes a gauge.json manifest, gauge-cases/ , and guidance in AGENTS.md . Commit those shared files. Keep .gauge/ private: it contains durable measurements and analyses. The Gauge skill teaches your coding agent where to find the CLI's instructions: gauge install-skill How the improvement loop works Hillclimbing means making a change, measuring whether it helped, and repeating. Skills and file inputs are read from your working tree. For an npm CLI or SDK, build and pack a new tarball before rerunning. Gauge installs these pre-release artifacts in the test sessions, so you can validate a fix before publishing it. The CLI handles execution and evidence collection. In local mode, your coding agent authors the changes and analyzes the local results. Saved evals and preference prompts live in .gauge/gauge.sqlite locally or in your hosted organization. Shared file-based cases optionally live in gauge-cases/ ; gauge.json declares project inputs and automation. Both measurement sources support local and hosted execution, with the input differences described below. Start with a saved local eval; use a shared case when the task is ready for teammates or CI. Create skills/release-notes/SKILL.md : --- name : release-notes description : Write release notes for a new version in the team's format. --- Write RELEASE-NOTES.md with the version as its title, an Added section for new features, and a Fixed section for bug fixes. Use one bullet per change. For a fresh project, use this gauge.json : { "version" : 2 , "inputs" : { "release-notes" : { "type" : " skill " , "path" : " skills/release-notes " } } } Save the task and criteria: gauge eval create --local --name " Release notes " \ --agent codex --samples 1 \ --text " Write the release notes for version 1.2.0. We added dark mode and fixed a login crash. " \ --criterion " Team format: RELEASE-NOTES.md has a version 1.2.0 title, dark mode under Added, and the login crash fix under Fixed. " Use the returned eval ID to preview, then launch when ready: gauge run --eval < eval-id > --local --input release-notes --dry-run gauge run --eval < eval-id > --local --input release-notes gauge instructions session-analysis --local The preview checks local readiness without launching an agent. Your coding agent then reads the session and publishes its analysis. After changing the Skill, rerun the same eval ID: the new batch snapshots the current input files while the baseline remains intact. Keep the task, criteria, and model pin fixed, analyze both batches, then compare: gauge run --eval < eval-id > --local --input release-notes gauge run compare --local --baseline batch= < before-id > --candidate batch= < after-id > For a choice study, use gauge preference create --kind open-ended with a task that lets the agent choose its approach, then gauge run --preference <id> . Supplying the Skill measures choice after that exposure, not discovery on the web. For a shared or automated version of the eval, use the same input configuration and create gauge-cases/release-notes/basic.md : --- criteria : - name : Release notes follow the team format rubric : RELEASE-NOTES.md has a version 1.2.0 title, dark mode under Added, and the login crash fix under Fixed. config : agents : - agent : CODEX_CLI sampleCount : 1 inputs : [release-notes] --- Write the release notes for version 1.2.0. We added dark mode and fixed a login crash. This case uses Codex; use CLAUDE_CODE , PI , or OPENCODE to test another harness with its configured credentials. The agent starts in an empty workspace with the Skill installed. The task does not explicitly tell it to use the Skill, so the session also reveals whether it discovers the guidance. gauge run --verify --local gauge run --dry-run --local gauge run --local gauge run list --local -o json Verification checks the config and cases. The dry run previews the sessions and checks local runtime and credential readiness. Neither launches an agent. Results, transcripts, and available diffs stay under .gauge/ . Have your coding agent follow gauge instructions session-analysis --local to assess each criterion and report friction with supporting evidence. After editing the Skill, rerun the case: gauge run --local --files " gauge-cases/release-notes/*.md " gauge run compare --local --baseline batch= < before-id > --candidate batch= < after-id > Use the batch IDs printed by the runs. The comparison summarizes completion, available turns/duration, and published criterion judgments. Read the findings and evidence to determine whether the fix worked. Gauge helps teams improve how AI agents discover, choose, and use their products. Agent Experience measures whether agents can successfully use your product. Agent Preference examines which tools agents choose for a task and why. This CLI puts that work in the terminal where you and your coding agent already work. Local execution supports the complete evaluate, analyze, fix, and retest loop. The hosted platform adds managed infrastructure and shared measurement over time. Sign in with gauge auth login to use hosted Chat and Agents. On a remote terminal, use gauge auth login --device . See signing in for help with login and API keys. Web fixtures let you test changes to content an agent encounters, such as a docs page, without publishing them first. They replace pages or route a site to a preview in both local and hosted runs. Hosted Gauge's gateway also brokers credentials and can rewrite responses separately for each session. Project inputs on saved eval/preference launches, and --dry-run for those saved measurements, are currently local-only. For hosted working-tree input snapshots and previews, use case files or a case spec with gauge run --hosted . For example, the shared case above supports gauge run --hosted --dry-run ; hosted previews contact Gauge and may upload inputs. Local and hosted saved measurements have separate IDs and storage. To move a project to hosted execution: gauge onboard gauge init --hosted gauge instructions --hosted gauge onboard signs you in and creates or selects a workspace. gauge init --hosted changes this checkout's private backend preference; it does not move local measurements or history into hosted storage. Hosted runs use workspace credits. See the documentation for hosted setup, PR checks, and optimization workflows. The CLI bundles instructions for coding agents, so the guidance matches the installed version: gauge instructions gauge instructions init gauge instructions run gauge instructions eval gauge instructions preference gauge instructions session-analysis gauge instructions --list gauge --help gauge run --help Use -o json on read commands for scripts and agent analysis. Check the runtime with gauge local runtime inspect ; configure provider credentials with gauge local profiles --help . Update the CLI with gauge update . See the CLI reference for configuration, supported inputs, credentials, background runs, cleanup, and CI usage. The installed CLI collects command usage by default: command name, timestamp, CLI version, and a random installation ID. It excludes arguments, prompts, file contents, and account identifiers. Disable collection with: gauge telemetry disable Or set GAUGE_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 for a process or CI environment. See telemetry details for storage, delivery, and the distinction from authenticated API usage analytics. From the repository root: npm ci npm ci --prefix cli npm run check check builds, typechecks, runs tests, and verifies packaged installs. It does not require a Gauge account, Docker, a database, or another repository checkout. For a CLI development loop after building, use npm run dev --prefix cli -- --help . Docker integration checks run in the custom runtime workflow . The runtime and CLI release workflows validate and publish versioned artifacts. Runtime releases produce a qualified manifest; commit it as cli/runtime-manifest.json before releasing the CLI. The shared libraries also have public npm releases, published by the agent adapters and local execution workflows from gauge-sh/gauge-cli . Each package's npm trusted publisher must point to that repository and its matching workflow. See Releasing for repository setup, package permissions, and the runtime-to-CLI release sequence. Issues are welcome. Forking and building your own version is the preferred way to customize Gauge. Only the Gauge team merges changes into this repository; we periodically consider bringing community changes upstream. See CONTRIBUTING.md . For account questions or private reports, contact support@withgauge.com . MIT .
